fixes.fix: Explained "What do you know about As of 2026, the army-technology.com stated that "the Irish Air Corp"
fixes.text:
VERDICT: The Royal Air Force (RAF) is relied upon for interception missions against suspicious aircraft over Ireland.
WHY: As of 2026, army-technology.com reported that the Irish Air Corps cannot detect or intercept aircraft with transponders off, leaving Ireland de facto dependent on the UK for air defence.
TRAPS: Do not confuse Irish Air Corps' non‑military roles (aid to civil power, maritime patrol) with air defence; the gap is specifically in interception capability.
HOOK: Remember "Ireland'

fixes.page: archive (Indian Aviation & Shipping / Indian Aviation & Shipping)
fixes.fix: Explained "The Air Corps (Irish: An tAerchór) is the air force of _____"
fixes.text: VERDICT: The Air Corps (An tAerchór) is the air force of Ireland. WHY: It is the aerial wing of the Defence Forces of Ireland, operating fixed‑wing aircraft and helicopters alongside the Army, Naval Service and Garda. TRAPS: Confusing it with the Royal Air Force (UK) or the Irish Naval Aviation (non‑existent) misses the specific national designation. HOOK: Imagine the green‑clad Irish pilots soaring over the Emerald Isle – on exam day, never mix up Ireland’s Air Corps with Britain’s RAF.

fixes.page: archive (Indian Aviation & Shipping / Indian Aviation & Shipping)
fixes.fix: Explained "The headquarters of the Air Corps is located at the _____ in Baldonnel, County Dublin"
fixes.text: VERDICT: The headquarters of the Air Corps is at Casement Aerodrome, Baldonnel, County Dublin. WHY: Casement Aerodrome is the sole military airbase of the Irish Air Corps, hosting its headquarters, training, and operational squadrons since 1922. TRAPS: Do not confuse with Dublin Airport (civilian) or Shannon Airport (transatlantic hub). The name "Baldonnel" is often used metonymically for the base, but the official designation is Casement Aerodrome. HOOK: Remember "Casement" — named after Roger
